events.description: Work never returns, exits its goroutine, or panics, or submitter abandons interest.
upstream_guards: Request runs in caller goroutine. No context in Execute.

events.description: Slow completion or submission, later overlapping request, and elapsed deadline while work remains outstanding.
upstream_guards: Direct API supplies no deadline for the workload.

events.description: A second Execute from the same caller while the first is pending, or after it returns and the caller still owns its result.
upstream_guards: No caller identity. A completed Execute returns the payload, with no release API.

events.description: Nil request, a call on the wrong valid breaker, or a nil or unconstructed receiver. Receiver selection differs from erroneous report payload.
upstream_guards: Go types do not enforce instance ownership or construction.

events.description: Attempt arrives late, or caller stops before or during submission, or after receiving the completion callback.
upstream_guards: No context and no teardown operation are supplied.

events.description: Same caller issues a second Allow before the first returns, or after the first returns while it still holds its callback.
upstream_guards: No caller identity or lock fairness guarantee.

events.description: Report omitted after an accepted trial, including logical teardown by caller.
upstream_guards: Public contract expects a report and supplies no cancellation API.

events.description: Outcome after generation rollover, elapsed expiry, or application cancellation. Success and failure are separate outcomes.
upstream_guards: No public API invalidates a report on application cancellation alone.

events.description: Same completion repeated sequentially or concurrently with equal or contradictory Booleans.
upstream_guards: No public contract specifies an exactly-once guarantee.

events.description: Unsolicited completion without admission, including invoking a nil callback returned with rejection.
upstream_guards: A non-nil callback must come from successful Allow. A caller can invoke nil in Go.

events.description: A valid but wrong Boolean, a callback reused for another request, or trip policy using an unintentionally misleading ratio.
upstream_guards: Outcome truth is not independently verified.

events.description: Missing, late, repeated, or interleaved read of state, counts or name.
upstream_guards: Public calls have no snapshot protocol spanning methods.

events.description: Classifier panics, blocks, or exits the goroutine.
upstream_guards: No failure or latency guarantee in Settings.

events.description: Classification finishes after generation changed, or re-enters the breaker before committing its result.
upstream_guards: No reentrancy restriction in Settings.

events.description: Trip callback panics, blocks, exits, or re-enters mutex-taking methods.
upstream_guards: No failure, latency or reentrancy guarantee in Settings.

events.description: Observer absent, panics, blocks, exits, or re-enters mutex-taking methods.
upstream_guards: Optional hook. No failure, latency or reentrancy guarantee in Settings.

events.description: Repeated same-named transitions across cycles or instances, or consumer misattributes the notification. Unsolicited callback invocation is possible outside the breaker by whoever owns the function.
upstream_guards: No unique identifier or event sequence number.

events.description: Deadline elapses without a qualifying call, delayed observation, equality at deadline, or clock time differs from intended schedule.
upstream_guards: No caller can deliver clock payload directly.

events.description: Construction omitted, or two calls create independently configured instances when one was intended.
upstream_guards: Creation allocates a fresh instance.

events.description: Negative durations or valid but unintended large request limit, interval or timeout.
upstream_guards: Constructor receives values after Go type checking.

remembrance: Observed-in-code: admissions consume a counter until a generation reset gobreaker.go:289 ("cb.counts.onRequest()") and gobreaker.go:365 ("cb.counts.clear()"). Generation is a uint64 gobreaker.go:128 ("generation uint64"). Request result and returned callback are caller-owned. A retained closure keeps its receiver and generation available gobreaker.go:272 ("tscb.cb.afterRequest(generation, success)"). Breaker stores no per-request history; equality check at gobreaker.go:299 ("if generation != before {"). Lifetime and memory use depend on external references.
lock_discipline: Observed-in-code: State gobreaker.go:207 ("cb.mutex.Lock()"), Counts gobreaker.go:217 ("cb.mutex.Lock()"), admission gobreaker.go:277 ("cb.mutex.Lock()"), and completion gobreaker.go:294 ("cb.mutex.Lock()") take the same mutex. Trip policy gobreaker.go:326 ("if cb.readyToTrip(cb.counts) {") and transition observer gobreaker.go:359 ("cb.onStateChange(cb.name, prev, state)") execute in these paths. Request and classifier execute outside the mutex gobreaker.go:242 ("result, err := req()") and gobreaker.go:243 ("cb.afterRequest(generation, cb.isSuccessful(err))"). Settings contracts README.md:53-63 specify neither reentrancy nor panic policy.
notes: Execute and Allow are alternate public front ends on their respective constructed instances. The internal outcome events describe bookkeeping phases, and do not denote independently callable operations.
